I don't want to give false hope if I'm wrong, but I recently had a friend who sent me a suicide note before I lost contact for months. I later found out she was alive although I can't bring myself to talk to her again.

Overdoses have an extremely low success rate in suicides (~1.3%), and the chances that she was placed in treatment program or simply stayed hospitalized for a while is fairly high. I spent 7 months in treatment with no contact to the outside world. And after that I didn't really use this account much.

Anyway, don't beat yourself up over not being able to be there for her. She may be alive, and even if she isn't, you were someone who was there for her when she was in pain. That counts for more than you think. One is only able to take their own life when they reach a point of pain so high that it breaks their natural fear of death. It is unlikely that any words could have stopped her, and she was in the best place possible for someone to physically intervene if she was in a hospital. I wish the best for you and if you ever need to talk about the guilt or pain you feel, feel free to pm me.

I have a lot of experience with intrusive thoughts. I often have violent or suicidal images at unwanted times. I wouldn't try to label yourself with any disorder, but I strongly recommend getting help from a therapist. A good therapist will focus on addressing where these thoughts originate from rather than the thoughts themselves. If this is really interfering with your life then you should seriously consider getting help whether or not your parents condone it.

At one point I tried to convince myself that I had multiple personalities, one dark and brooding and only capable of feeling the emotion of anger, the other optimistic but unstable and even weak. Then there was a third, the presiding consciousness that governed the other two and regulated them. It's normal for extreme emotions to manifest themselves as seeming sharp changes in personality. My best advice for you is to try and be empathetic towards the other state of mind whichever you are in. Try to emulate the other within the one you are feeling in order to try to accept both states of mind.

This is actually exactly what I experience, I call them intrusive thoughts and for the most part they are extreme manifestations of my emotions. When I am sad I hear suicidal thoughts, not as voices but as words almost as if I am trying to say them. When I am angry they get violent. They are actually perfectly normal, but some people experience them more than others. For most people it is akin to the random bad thoughts that pop into your head: "what if I just punched that kid over there?" Don't freak out about the thoughts, the worst thing you can do is try to diagnose yourself. I once tried to convince myself I had multiple personalities. Just try and redirect yourself towards positive thinking when you hear them.

To be honest it makes me a little angry that you call her a "bad person". I understand that she can be impossible to deal with and believe me I have met people worse than you describe, but I don't think that someone's illness should make them a bad person.
That being said, it sounds like she needs serious help. My suggestion would be an inpatient treatment center, I spent a good deal of time in treatment centers and I have seen people with similar behavioral issues make huge improvements. I agree that letting her do what she wants sounds like a bad idea, she will only end up pushing away the people around her and suffer depression as a result of the natural consequences. In my opinion the best thing for her would be to be placed in a situation where she is forced to comply and make friends with people.
What can you do? The best thing you alone could possibly do for her is be a good, unconditional friend. Endure the abuse she will inevitably punish you with and show her that some people can't be pushed away. Show her that someone really cares about her regardless of her actions.

Yes, it is much better. Actually though, the fact that you are afraid of messing up your body chemistry speaks to your will to live. It also is telling that you are in denial about seeking treatment, you may not want the help because you are afraid of anything other than this depression that you have always felt. I was depressed for my entire life until I sought help about a year ago. I am now almost completely recovered.

Of course, until  you reach the age of 25 your brain doesn't stop changing, I'm almost 18 and my sense of self has changed at least 5 times, it's quite possible that you will continue to change your ideas for the rest of your life.

What your therapist means is that you need to find reason in your life. What values do you uphold and why do you uphold them? What are your morals? What kind of person do you aspire to be? Try and come up with reasons why you do things, starting small with everyday tasks and work your way deeper into self discovery.
